quests.instruction: The wind is so cold that Ravi's teeth chatter and his shoulders shake. He ___ in the cold.
quests.hint: Cold makes the whole body do something small and quick.
quests.explanation: Shiver means to shake slightly because you are cold or frightened.
quests.funFact: Shivering is one way the body makes heat when it is cold.

quests.instruction: The roof has a small crack, and after the rain, water ___ slowly from the ceiling into a bucket.
quests.hint: One small drop falls at a time.
quests.explanation: Drip means to fall in small drops.
quests.funFact: A tap that drips once a second wastes thousands of litres of water in a year.

quests.instruction: After the storm, the sun comes out, and by lunchtime the puddles on the road have started to ___.
quests.hint: Water leaves the ground little by little.
quests.explanation: Dry up means to lose all water and become dry. Puddles dry up when the sun heats them.
quests.funFact: Water does not disappear; it rises into the air as vapour.

quests.instruction: Grandma presses the dough with the heels of her hands and folds it over again and again to make bread. She ___ it.
quests.hint: The dough must be pushed and folded.
quests.explanation: Knead means to press and fold dough with your hands. It makes the bread soft.
quests.funFact: Kneading helps flour and water form gluten, which gives bread its stretchy texture.

quests.instruction: Before the cake goes into the oven, Mia takes tiny pinches of sugar and lets them fall all over the top. She ___ sugar on it.
quests.hint: Tiny amounts fall from her fingers.
quests.explanation: Sprinkle means to scatter small drops or pieces of something over a surface.
quests.funFact: The tiny coloured sweets on cakes are called sprinkles because they are sprinkled on top.

quests.instruction: Tom has a ball of dough and a stick, and he presses the stick over it to make a flat circle for a chapati. He ___ the dough out.
quests.hint: A wooden stick moves back and forth over the dough.
quests.explanation: Roll out means to flatten something by pushing a roller over it.
quests.funFact: A rolling pin is a cylinder, so it spreads pressure evenly across the dough.

quests.instruction: Before the card game, Hana mixes all the cards so no one knows their order. She ___ the cards.
quests.hint: The cards must end up in a random order.
quests.explanation: Shuffle means to mix cards so that they are in a random order.
quests.funFact: A deck of 52 cards can be arranged in so many ways that a well-shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order that has never existed before.

quests.instruction: In turn, Ravi gives out five cards to each player around the table. He ___ the cards.
quests.hint: Each player gets some.
quests.explanation: Deal means to give out cards to the players in a game.
quests.funFact: 'Deal' can also mean a bargain, as in 'It's a good deal.'

quests.instruction: When the teacher is not looking, Sam secretly looks at Ali's paper to find an answer. Sam is ___.
quests.hint: He is breaking the rules.
quests.explanation: Cheat means to break the rules to get an advantage.
quests.funFact: Most sports have a referee to make sure that the players follow the rules.

quests.instruction: In a cricket match, Dev runs up and throws the ball toward the batter. He ___.
quests.hint: The player at the other end tries to hit his ball.
quests.explanation: Bowl means to throw the ball in cricket toward the batter.
quests.funFact: In cricket, the person who bowls usually takes a run-up before the throw.

quests.instruction: In the same match, Arjun stands in front of the wickets with a bat in his hand, ready to hit the ball. He ___.
quests.hint: His job is to hit the ball.
quests.explanation: Bat means to hit the ball with a bat in cricket or baseball.
quests.funFact: 'Bat' is also the name of a flying animal, but the two meanings are unrelated.

quests.instruction: After the ball is hit, Priya runs and catches it before it touches the ground. She ___.
quests.hint: She is on the team that is trying to stop runs.
quests.explanation: Field means to stop and catch or throw the ball when it has been hit.
quests.funFact: In cricket, there are usually eleven players on each side.

quests.instruction: At the airport, Mum shows the tickets at the desk to say that the family has arrived. She ___ for the flight.
quests.hint: This is done before going through security.
quests.explanation: Check in means to tell the airline that you have arrived at the airport and get your boarding pass.
quests.funFact: Many airlines now let you check in online before you leave home.

quests.instruction: To stop a taxi, Dad stands at the roadside and raises his arm. He ___ a taxi.
quests.hint: He is signalling to the driver.
quests.explanation: Hail means to signal to a taxi or a bus to stop.
quests.funFact: 'Hail' is also frozen rain that falls from the sky.

quests.instruction: When the holiday ends and they are back at home, Mum takes everything out of the suitcases. She ___.
quests.hint: It is the opposite of what she did before the trip.
quests.explanation: Unpack means to take things out of a bag or suitcase. It is the opposite of pack.
quests.funFact: 'Un-' is a small piece at the start of a word that often means 'the opposite of'.

quests.instruction: At the market, the seller puts the mangoes on the scale to find out how heavy they are. He ___ them.
quests.hint: He finds out how heavy they are.
quests.explanation: Weigh means to find out how heavy something is. 'Weigh' can also describe how heavy something is.
quests.funFact: A litre of water weighs about one kilogram.

quests.instruction: Aisha thinks the price of the bag is too high, so she asks the seller for a smaller price. She ___.
quests.hint: She talks about the price before she pays.
quests.explanation: Bargain means to talk about the price to try to pay less.
quests.funFact: In many markets around the world, bargaining is expected.

quests.instruction: There are ten people ahead of Kofi at the ticket window, so he waits in the line. He ___.
quests.hint: He is standing one behind another.
quests.explanation: Queue means to stand in a line and wait. In American English, people say 'wait in line'.
quests.funFact: 'Queue' is spelled with five letters, but it sounds just like the letter 'Q'.

quests.instruction: Dad wraps the blanket snugly around the little girl's body when she gets in bed. He ___ her in.
quests.hint: It is a loving bedtime action.
quests.explanation: Tuck in means to put covers around someone in bed so they feel snug.
quests.funFact: 'Tuck in' also means to start eating enthusiastically.

quests.instruction: When Anu falls asleep on the sofa, Mum gently presses her lips to her forehead. She ___ Anu.
quests.hint: It is a soft, loving touch.
quests.explanation: Kiss means to touch someone with your lips as a sign of love or a greeting.
quests.funFact: In some countries, people kiss on the cheek to say hello.

quests.instruction: Max left his wet towel on the bed again, and Mum speaks to him angrily. She ___ him.
quests.hint: She tells him off for something wrong.
quests.explanation: Scold means to tell someone off in an angry way for something they did wrong.
quests.funFact: A gentle reminder often works better than a scolding.

quests.instruction: Leo and Sam had a fight on Monday, but today they say sorry and are friends again. They ___.
quests.hint: It is the opposite of a quarrel.
quests.explanation: Make up means to become friends again after an argument.
quests.funFact: 'Make up' also means to invent a story, or to put on make-up.

quests.instruction: Some boys begin to tease the new girl, but Nina says, 'Stop it. Leave her alone!' She ___ the girl.
quests.hint: She takes the side of someone who needs help.
quests.explanation: Stand up for means to defend someone or something.
quests.funFact: Standing up for someone can take a lot of courage.

quests.instruction: Zoe is sad because her drawing was not picked for the prize. Her friend tells a funny joke to make her feel better. She ___ her up.
quests.hint: She helps her feel happy again.
quests.explanation: Cheer up means to make someone feel happier, or to become happier yourself.
quests.funFact: 'Cheer up!' is something you say to a friend who looks sad.

quests.instruction: In the evening, the lamp in Rina's room keeps going on and off in little flashes. It ___.
quests.hint: The light is not steady.
quests.explanation: Flicker means to shine in an unsteady way, going on and off quickly.
quests.funFact: A candle flame flickers when there is a gentle draught.

quests.instruction: Dad forgot to turn off the tap, and the bath is so full that water is spilling over the edge. The bath is ___.
quests.hint: There is more water than the bath can hold.
quests.explanation: Overflow means to flow over the top of something because it is too full.
quests.funFact: Rivers overflow after heavy rain.

quests.instruction: The old wooden door makes a long, squeaky sound when Ben pushes it open. The door ___.
quests.hint: It is a noise old wood makes.
quests.explanation: Creak means to make a long, high, squeaky sound, like an old door or floor.
quests.funFact: Houses often creak as the wood warms and cools through the day.

quests.instruction: The puzzle looks impossible, but Priya studies the pieces, tries different ideas and slowly works out the answer. She ___ it out.
quests.hint: Her thinking leads to the answer.
quests.explanation: Figure out means to find the answer to a problem by thinking about it.
quests.funFact: 'Figure out' is a very common way to say 'work out' in everyday speech.

quests.instruction: After trying the same thing ten times without success, Ravi stops trying and walks away. He ___.
quests.hint: He quits.
quests.explanation: Give up means to stop trying because something is too hard.
quests.funFact: Some of the best inventors tried many times before they found success.

quests.instruction: Before submitting, Hana looks at her answers a second time to make sure that nothing is wrong. She ___ them.
quests.hint: She looks again just to be sure.
quests.explanation: Double-check means to check something a second time to make sure it is right.
quests.funFact: Checking twice is a habit shared by pilots, doctors and careful students.
